title: Nature & Propagation of Light — 15 MCQs
description: Huygens' Principle — reflection & refraction. 15 MCQs with explanations. Select an answer and submit to view explanation and marking.

questions.q: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as:
options: A source of secondary spherical wavelets
questions.explanation: Huygens: each point on a wavefront may be considered a source of secondary wavelets; the new wavefront is the envelope of these wavelets.

questions.q: Using Huygens' construction, the reflected wavefront is obtained by taking:
options: Envelope of secondary wavelets in the region of reflection
questions.explanation: Reflected wavefront is the envelope of wavelets produced by points on the incident wavefront when reflection boundary conditions are applied.

questions.q: When applying Huygens' principle at a plane reflecting surface, the angle of reflection equals:
options: Sum of incidence and transmission angles
questions.explanation: The construction yields reflected ray making same angle with the normal as incident ray — law of reflection.

questions.q: Huygens' principle can be used to derive Snell's law for refraction by considering:
options: Different speeds of secondary wavelets in the two media
questions.explanation: In refraction, secondary wavelets travel at different speeds in the two media; envelope construction leads to sin θ1 / sin θ2 = v1 / v2 = n2 / n1 (Snell's law).

questions.q: In Huygens' explanation of refraction, what is conserved across the boundary for a monochromatic wave?
questions.explanation: Frequency is determined by the source and remains the same across boundary; wavelength and speed change.

questions.q: If sound waves travel from air into water, Huygens' construction predicts that the refracted wavefront in water is:
options: Closer spaced (shorter wavelength) because speed is lower in water?
questions.explanation: If wave speed in water is higher than in air, spacing increases; for sound typically water speed is higher so wavelength increases; general answer depends on v2 vs v1. The principle: spacing ∝ speed (wavelength = v/f).

questions.q: Huygens' principle explains why rays in reflection obey the law of reflection because the envelope of secondary wavelets is tangent to:
options: Wavelets symmetric about normal leading to equal angles
questions.explanation: Symmetry of contributions about the normal at a planar surface leads to equal incidence and reflection angles.

questions.q: When a plane wavefront meets a boundary obliquely and the speed in medium 2 is lower than in medium 1, the refracted ray bends:
questions.explanation: If v2 < v1 then sinθ2 = (v2/v1) sinθ1 < sinθ1 ⇒ θ2 < θ1, so ray bends toward the normal.

questions.q: Huygens' principle alone does not fully explain intensity distribution; to account for amplitude and energy one supplements it with:
options: Fresnel's construction (and Huygens–Fresnel principle) including phase and amplitude weighting
questions.explanation: Huygens–Fresnel principle adds phase and amplitude contributions (including obliquity factor) to predict diffraction and interference intensities.

questions.q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from medium 1 to medium 2 and:
options: Incidence angle exceeds critical angle because sinθ_c = n2/n1 (n1>n2)
questions.explanation: TIR: when n1>n2 and θ_incident > θ_c (sin θ_c = n2/n1), refraction cannot satisfy Snell's law so wave is totally reflected.

questions.q: Using Huygens, the critical angle for total internal reflection arises because secondary wavelets in the second medium:
options: Cannot form an advancing envelope into the second medium for larger angles
questions.explanation: Beyond critical angle, the construction cannot produce a real refracted ray in medium 2 — transmitted wave becomes evanescent (no propagating envelope), leading to TIR.

questions.q: A plane wave traveling in medium A with speed v_A strikes interface to medium B with speed v_B. Snell's law from Huygens yields:
questions.explanation: From geometry of wavelets and common frequency: λ ∝ v so sinθ_A / sinθ_B = λ_A/λ_B = v_A/v_B; equivalently n_B/n_A = sinθ_A / sinθ_B.

questions.q: A light ray from glass (n=1.5) to air (n=1.0) will have critical angle approximately:
When a spherical wavefront emerges from a point source and reaches a plane interface, Huygens' construction of transmitted wavefront relies on:
options: Drawing secondary wavelets in second medium with reduced/increased radii according to new speed
questions.explanation: Each point on incident wavefront emits secondary wavelets in medium 2 whose radii grow with speed v2; the envelope yields refracted wavefront.

questions.q: Which of these phenomena can be directly predicted by Huygens–Fresnel construction (wavelets + interference)?
options: Diffraction patterns (and direction of refracted/reflected beams)
Only ray direction with no diffraction
questions.explanation: Huygens–Fresnel principle (with phase and amplitude superposition) predicts diffraction and interference, beyond simple geometric refraction/reflection.
